## Destination

Implement all twelve decisions from [map #1](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/1) to production-ready completion — a Laravel 13 + PHP 8.5 application presenting Chinook, Northwind, and Sakila as three sample products within one application, with an Admin Filament 5 panel plus one Filament 5 panel per product, hybrid search via FTS5 + sqlite-vec v0.1.9, Spatie Permission + Shield authorization, reproducible Product Import and independent Product Reset, and the version-controlled Implementation-Readiness Dossier — passing the Two-Environment Operational Gate (Linux x86_64 CI green on every PR; Herd macOS arm64 CLI + HTTP evidence on each release candidate), Larastan at the target level, comprehensive Pest coverage, and proportional documentation per the software documentation lifecycle.

## Notes

- **Source of plan:** [map #1](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/1) and its twelve child decisions ([#2](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/2)–[#13](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/13)). [Issue #11](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/11) defines the eight Acceptance Stages and six mandatory evidence types — they are the spine of this map.
- **Domain glossary:** [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) — especially *Acceptance Gate*, *Acceptance Stage*, *Acceptance Evidence*, *Baseline Evidence Fixture*, *Reset Isolation Proof*, *Authorization Acceptance Matrix*, *Golden Search Corpus*, *Two-Environment Operational Gate*, *Implementation-Readiness Dossier*.
- **Plan-only mode:** each ticket resolves ONE decision; execution is handed off once the way is clear. No ticket carries implementation into itself.
- **Skills every session should consult:** `wayfinder`, `laravel-best-practices`, `pest-testing`, `livewire-development`, `fluxui-development`, `fortify-development`, `tailwindcss-development`; plus `domain-modeling` / `grilling` / `prototype` / `research` as the ticket type dictates.
- **Verify version-sensitive claims** against official Laravel 13, Livewire 4, Filament 5, sqlite-vec v0.1.9, and upstream sample-dataset sources. Issues #2, #3, #4 pinned these — do not re-litigate without a recorded reason.
- **DATABASE TIER (pivot recorded 2026-07-20):** the application uses **PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector + tsvector** — not SQLite. Resolving #21 revealed Herd's stock PHP PDO build cannot load sqlite-vec (T2.1/T2.4 findings), and the operator pivoted the entire DB tier to PostgreSQL, which is already running locally. This re-opens decisions #3 (sqlite-vec → pgvector), partially #6 (schema dialect), and #12 (SQLite extension bootstrap → Postgres extension management). New tickets: [#40](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) (stack), [#41](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) (schema), [#42](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) (extensions). Closed as out of scope: [#21](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) (T2.2 Extension Connection Gate), [#22](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22) (T2.3 Vector Capability Probe). Decisions #2, #4, #5, #7, #8, #9, #10, #13 unchanged.
- **Each ticket sized to one 100K-token agent session;** claim by assigning to the driver before any work.
- **Repo state at chart time:** bootstrapped (Laravel 13.17, PHP 8.5, Livewire teams starter with Fortify + Flux 2 + passkeys + 2FA + teams, Pest 4, Larastan 3, Pint, Boost, pnpm/Vite, `tests.yml` workflow, composer scripts for `lint` / `lint:check` / `types:check` / `test` / `ci:check`). **Not yet installed:** Filament 5, Spatie Permission/Shield. **Database tier (pivot, stack selected via #40):** Herd-managed PostgreSQL 18.x + pgvector 0.8.x + pg_trgm + unaccent on `127.0.0.1:5437` (service name `Herd_PostgreSQL`, DB `laravel`, user `root`); `pdo_pgsql` loaded in Herd's PHP. No domain code yet.

## Decisions so far

- [Pivot to PostgreSQL + pgvector](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) — Resolving [#21 (T2.2 Extension Connection Gate)](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) revealed (via T2.1 / T2.4 research) that Herd's stock PHP PDO build cannot load sqlite-vec. The operator pivoted the entire DB tier to PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector (already running locally). Dissolves the Extension Connection Gate / Native Extension Fault / SQLite Extension Manifest / Vector Capability Probe concepts. Re-opens decisions #3, #6, #12 via three new tickets: [#40](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) (stack), [#41](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) (schema), [#42](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) (extensions). [#22 (T2.3)](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22) closed in parallel.
- [PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) — Herd-managed PG 18.x + pgvector 0.8.x (Herd-bundled; patch-drift follows Herd's release cadence). HNSW index with pgvector defaults (`m=16`, `ef_construction=64`, query-time `ef_search=40`) for the 1,536-dim `text-embedding-3-small` profile from #8. tsvector config: `english` + `unaccent` via custom `en_unaccent` text search configuration; `ts_rank_cd` ranking with ABCD field weights (D=title/name, C=description, B=category, A=identifier). Extensions: `vector`, `unaccent`, `pg_trgm`. - [Larastan max-violation gate policy resolved](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/15#issuecomment-5049312286) — Keep `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules` (operator's deliberate `a91c5b0` choice); one permanent framework-idiom carve-out for `staticMethod.dynamicCall` (61 violations — structurally incompatible with Eloquent's query builder API: `Model::where()`, `$relation->exists()`, etc.); fix all 82 remaining violations in code (zero additional carve-outs). **Policy refinement to #17:** permanent framework-idiom carve-outs are exempt from the retiring-ticket citation requirement — they carry a `# framework-idiom:` comment instead, reviewed on framework/PHPStan major version bumps. **Nullable-safety fix approach:** `assert(auth()->check())` guards in tests (35 sites) — narrows type for PHPStan, preserves loud TypeError on unexpected failures (not nullsafe `?->` which silently returns null). **#18 factual correction:** the "0 violations at max" premise was true before `a91c5b0` added strict-rules companion packages, false after; policy (`level: max`, no baseline) stands. **143 violations fully categorized:** strict-rules 85 (61 carved-out `staticMethod.dynamicCall` + 24 fixed: boolean strictness 17, arrayFilter/empty/ternary/function.strict 7), core nullable-safety 36 (fixed via bd `.3`), peststan 7 (fixed — add param types), core type issues 15 (fixed — argument.type/return.type/etc.) — the 46 non-nullable fixes tracked in bd `.4`. **Bead restructuring:** `.3` stays scoped to nullable-safety (36, assert-guard approach); new `.4` covers remaining 46; `.1` closes when both land + `types:check` exits 0 + `ignoreErrors` block with the `staticMethod.dynamicCall` carve-out added to `phpstan.neon`. **Verification command:** `XDEBUG_MODE=off php -d xdebug.mode=off vendor/phpstan/phpstan/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M --no-progress`. Refines #18 (factual premise corrected, policy stands), #17 (framework-idiom carve-out exemption), T8.3 (Xdebug verification command pinned).
- [Spatie + Shield + Fortify + Team co-existence boundary selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/26) — **Spatie is the sole capability/RBAC engine; the starter's `TeamRole`/`TeamPermission` are reframed as membership-position data on `team_members`, not a rival RBAC; Spatie `teams` mode OFF** (verified against Spatie v7 docs: `teams` is a tenant-style permission-scoping axis via `setPermissionsTeamId()`, contradicting CONTEXT.md's anti-tenant glossary). full teams-mode consolidation rejected (~51 vs ~87 weighted — re-opens #16's "untouched starter" baseline, churns tested code under #17/#18 strict gates, redundant with the existing `belongsToMany` membership); (2) **role taxonomy** — `super_admin` = *System Operator* (Shield `Gate::before` bypass; subsumes curator), `{product}_curator` = per-product grants of the singular *Sample Curator* Global Capability, *Product Entitlement* = authenticated (never role-gated); CONTEXT.md gets a refinement note (Sample Curator granted per Sample Product; System Operator implies all); (3) **Filament↔Fortify coexistence source-verified (Filament v5.1.1)** — all four panels `->authGuard('web')`, omit `->login()`/registration/reset/verification, keep `Authenticate`; unauthenticated panel → `Panel::getLoginUrl()` returns `null` → `Authenticate::redirectTo()` → framework `?? route('login')` → Fortify `/login` (no `RouteNotFoundException`); `canAccessPanel()` per-panel gate (#16 match pattern, docs-blessed); Fortify `LoginResponse` `redirect()->intended()` bounce-back free; **#19's "inferred, not blessed" uncertainty dissolved** at source level; 4-panel unauthenticated-redirect regression test → #17; (4) **Shield generation scope** — `shield:generate --panel=admin` only; `TeamPolicy.php` untouched (Team not a Filament Resource — starter Livewire SFC per anti-tenant stance); glossary boundary holds **by construction** (team-position is a pivot column, invisible to Shield, no UI guard); product-policy-namespace arch rule → #17; (5) **production operator onboarding** — `php artisan operator:create` (env-driven creds, `firstOrCreate` User + personal team + `super_admin`, writes a Supplementary Activity audit row per #13, fails loud if creds unset); **dev-seeding moves from #16's baseline-operator migration to `DatabaseSeeder`** (migrations shouldn't mint identities from secrets — refines #16's mechanism, honors intent); 2FA at first login; subsequent operators via RoleResource; (6) **team-context middleware unchanged** — `SetTeamUrlDefaults` stays global but inert for the four panel route trees (no `{current_team}`/`{team}` params declared → `URL::defaults` injects nothing); `EnsureTeamMembership` stays route-scoped to team routes, structurally cannot gate a panel; Product Entitlement never team-gated; (7) **Global Role Administration** — Shield `RoleResource` **runtime-manages** (create + assign) global roles under the convention `super_admin` + one `{product}_curator` per Sample Product; convention documented, **not code-locked** (#16's dynamic `canAccessPanel` `{$panel->getId()}_curator` pattern is the enabler for future samples); safeguards at the code layer: `super_admin` = role name + `Gate::before`; Import/Reset CLI-gated on `hasRole('super_admin')` (#28/#29), NOT Shield permissions (runtime grants cannot escalate curator→operator); team-position & Product Entitlement structurally unreachable. Refines #9 (Global Capability realized), #13 (Admin-only Shield + Supplementary Activity), #16 (Q3 path verified; Q5 migration→seeder), #17 (3 new shapes: 4-panel redirect test, product-policy-namespace arch rule, Authorization Matrix role×resource×panel cells). Dissolves #19 (dual-role-system forks + "inferred not blessed" coexistence). Unblocks #30 (Filament Resource generation) and #36 (Team Artefact).
- [Git branch, PR, and dependency-pinning strategy selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/39#issuecomment-5057908715) — Trunk-based + short-lived feature branches off `main`; one PR per execution-bead (bundle only atomically-dependent beads); squash merge with Conventional Commits PR titles; `delete_branch_on_merge` ON; operator-driven weekly isolated bump PRs per ecosystem (composer/npm) running #11's full gate, security advisories out-of-cycle, no incidental dep bumps in feature PRs; Dependabot expanded from github-actions-only to composer+npm(`pnpm-lock`)+github-actions grouped weekly (needs `config.platform.php=8.5`); **`act` rejected** — arm64-on-x86_64 mismatch + imperfect `setup-php`/`pgvector` service-container fidelity make it a non-authoritative third env, native `composer ci:check` loop + GitHub Actions is the gate per #11 (containerized local runner may graduate under T8.3). Execution follow-ups filed as bd `.5`–`.8` (repo settings, Dependabot config, conventions/PR template, shell-quote CVE); branch protection deferred to T8.3. Refines #11 (per-PR gate gets a branch+merge substrate + dep-bump PR shape), #15 (every bead has a defined PR shape), T8.3 (branch-protection settings, PR convention, deferred local-CI question).
- [Filament Resource generation strategy selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/30) — **Generator-first with per-panel routing.** Use `make:filament-resource {Entity} --panel={product} --model-namespace="App\\Domain\\{Product}\\Models" --generate` to scaffold each resource directly into the correct panel namespace (`app/Filament/{Panel}/Resources/`). Hand-edit for product-specific tailoring after generation. Panel ownership is implicit via filesystem namespace (no explicit `getPanel()` method). **Shield policy binding: panel-qualified permissions.** Run `shield:generate --panel={panel}` per panel; permissions named `{panel}_{entity}.{action}` (e.g., `chinook_album.view_any`). Roles compose from these: `{product}_curator` gets all `{product}_*` permissions; `super_admin` gets everything via `Gate::before`. Panel-qualified chosen over generic permissions because: (1) `view_any` controls nav visibility — generic permissions would render nav items in every panel; (2) isolation auditable at the permission level, not hidden in query scopes; (3) adding a new product = one `shield:generate --panel=newproduct` + one new `{product}_curator` role, zero code changes to existing resources; (4) aligns with Shield's design assumption of panel-scoped permission names. ~180-270 permissions across 3 products (manageable). **Rejected:** hand-rolled-from-start (repetitive boilerplate), hybrid clone-and-adapt (inconsistent skeletons), generic permissions + query scopes (leaky isolation, human-memory dependency for new products). Refines #5 (panel namespace generator-enforced), #13 (Shield admin-only + panel-qualified permissions), #26 (role taxonomy extended to per-resource permissions). Unblocks actual Filament resource generation (#16 execution).
- [Embedding Profile implementation selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/33) — **`laravel/ai` (first-party Laravel AI SDK) with OpenAI primary, OpenRouter free-model fallback, 1024d dimension re-pin.** Client: `composer require laravel/ai`; embeddings via `Embeddings::for([...])->dimensions(1024)->generate('openai', 'text-embedding-3-small')`. Providers configured in `config/ai.php` — OpenAI (primary, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) and OpenRouter (fallback, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `openai-compatible` driver at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`). Fallback is dormant today; activates when a free model at matching dimensions exists. **Dimension re-pin: 1024** (refines #8's 1536d) — OpenAI Matryoshka truncation (`dimensions: 1024`); free model `nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free` at 1024d is the working fallback today. Schema: `vector(1024)` not `vector(1536)`. `embedding_profile` string format: `{provider}:{model}:{dimensions}` (e.g., `openai:text-embedding-3-small:1024`). Content digest: SHA-256 of concatenated `weight_*_text` columns. Queue: database queue (existing `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`). After-commit listener: Eloquent observer on tier-1 source-entity models dispatches `EmbeddingJob` on `saved`. Verification: `embedding_state` lifecycle column + Baseline Invariant at end of Product Import/Reset (not after-commit re-verification — #32 retired that). Failure path: 3 retries with exponential backoff, then `embedding_state = 'failed'`; Admin diagnostics surface pending/failed counts; no infinite retry. **Rejected:** vanilla HTTP (too much boilerplate for one API call), `openai-php/client` directly (not first-party), OpenRouter as primary (same model, extra middleman, zero benefit), 1536d (free fallback models are 1024d; 1–3% quality loss is negligible for sample data). Refines #8 (dimension 1536→1024, provider scope extended), #32 (profile format + digest algorithm + vector dimension). Unblocks #34 (Hybrid Retrieval query contract) and execution tickets for `laravel/ai` install + `EmbeddingJob`.
- [Hybrid Retrieval (RRF) and Federated Search selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/34) — **Pure-PHP RRF, static-registry deep-links, federated `UNION ALL` across product schemas.** RRF implementation: pure PHP (~15 lines, no package dependency), k=60, top-50 candidates per path (lexical + semantic). Candidate lists: lexical via `ts_rank_cd(document_tsv, to_tsquery('en_unaccent', $1))` LIMIT 50; semantic via HNSW KNN `embedding vector_cosine_ops` with `SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = 40` LIMIT 50. Product-label preservation: literal `product_tenant` column in 3-way `UNION ALL` across `chinook`/`northwind`/`sakila` schemas (per #41). Deep-link routing: static registry maps `(product_tenant, entity_type)` → Filament Resource class; calls `Resource::getUrl('view', ['record' => $id], panel: $product)`. Tier participation: tier-2 rows (NULL embedding, `lexical_only`) excluded from HNSW automatically; tier-3 rows absent from `search_projections` entirely. **Rejected:** Scout driver or RRF package (abstraction for a one-line formula); convention-based resolution (fragile — renamed class breaks silently); route-stored-in-projection (stale if routes change, couples projection to routing). Closes the search-cluster wayfinder tickets (#31, #32, #33, #34 all resolved). Refines #8 (RRF parameters now have concrete implementation spec), #32 (query shape ties generated columns to retrieval path), #41 (federated `UNION ALL` with `product_tenant` labels is the concrete cross-schema query pattern). Unblocks execution: `ReciprocalRankFusion` class, `SearchDeepLinkRegistry`, federated search service, and Pest tests for rank fusion correctness.
- [Portfolio Card architecture selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/35) — **Filament Widget, Postgres view, single reusable class, three-column layout.** Component type: Filament Widget (extends `Filament\Widgets\Widget`) — already a Livewire component; gets dashboard grid, panel auth, stats-overview type for free. Snapshot storage: Postgres view (`public.product_portfolio_snapshots`) — always fresh, no update-path bugs, one `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` away from a table if needed. Card registration: single reusable `ProductPortfolioCard` widget class with `product` prop; registered three times in Admin panel provider (Chinook → Northwind → Sakila). Dashboard layout: three equal-width columns (`getColumns() → 3`), alphabetical sort. Operator vs Team layout deferred to #36. Refines #10 (Product Portfolio now has a concrete implementation shape), #13 (code-owned = Filament Widget classes in panel provider), #16 (Admin panel receives `->widgets([...])` + Dashboard page class). Unblocks execution: `ProductPortfolioCard` widget, `product_portfolio_snapshots` view migration, `ProductPortfolioSnapshot` Eloquent model, Admin Dashboard page class.
- [Team Artefact schema and Team Owner policy boundary selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/36) — Single polymorphic `team_artefacts` table (`type` enum `'saved_search'|'team_dashboard'`, nullable `configuration` jsonb, UUIDv7 PKs, `created_by` nullable FK SET NULL on user delete). Saved Search config = bookmarked query recipe (`query`, `products`, `filters`, `sort`, `result_limit`, soft cap); Team Dashboard config = ordered layout of Product Portfolio Cards (`cards[]`, `columns` 3 default). Attribution retained on membership end; user deletion SET NULLs FK. Team Owner authority: update/delete any team artefact, reassign attribution, restore soft-deleted (30d); cannot transfer teams, view other teams, or write sample data. Current-team scoping absolute via route context `/{current_team}/searches`. Saved Search integrates with Federated Search page as query pre-fill with auto-execution, `last_run_at` tracking, and fresh execution on run. Refines #9, #35, #26; supersedes partial #9.
- [Implementation-Readiness Dossier format and generation strategy selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/37) — Hand-reviewable Markdown committed under `docs/15-delivery/1515-implementation-readiness-dossier/` with path-derived prefixes (`151501-contents.md`, `151598-index.md`, stage files `151502`-`151517`). `php artisan dossier:generate` scaffolds stage files from #11 stages + Wayfinder #15 child issue metadata + `acceptance_criteria` with `> **OPERATOR TODO:**` and `> **EVIDENCE TODO:**` markers for human completion. Generated on demand or post-merge in CI; manual edits between markers preserved across re-generations. Navigation entry point = `151501-contents.md` (no separate README in folder). Stage file 7-section layout (guidance, gates, decisions, evidence, commands, recovery, notes). Refines #11, #15.
- [Documentation set per the software documentation lifecycle selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/38) — Full ADR for every resolved wayfinder decision (#2–#13, #19–#42) under `docs/10-architecture/1015-adrs/` (`php artisan adr:generate` scaffolded). README concise dev onboarding only (no operator commands or architecture rationale). Operator runbook folded into dossier stage files (no separate runbook). Stage status tracked exclusively in dossier. Proportional incremental delivery: each stage requires filled dossier file + written ADRs to be complete. Refines #11, #15.

## Not yet specified

- **All decisions across Stages 1–8 are now fully charted** — Wayfinder Map #15 has completed its decision-charting phase across all eight Acceptance Stages.
- Per-product variation (Chinook vs Northwind vs Sakila) in import, schema, and search may surface as product-specific decisions once the Chinook prototype (T4.4/T6.5 equivalents in execution) validates the architecture. Until then, the architecture is charted once for Chinook and applied by precedent to the other two products.
- Product Reset Recovery procedure detail — **resolved by #29**: the Reset Window write-blocking mechanism (app-layer `ResetWindow` service, single-connection-compatible — DB-level REVOKE structurally impossible under #41), Reset Evidence JSON schema (`schema_version: 1` + 9 sections + `failure.stack_hash`), Reset Confirmation signed-token protocol (new `public.reset_confirmations` table, 5min TTL, applies to `reset`/`recover`/`--force` not `first_import`/`--dry-run`), and recovery runbook (operator decision tree keyed off `remediation_hint` enum + resume-from-failed-phase semantics + child-run linkage via `recovery_of`) are now all pinned. No further wayfinder decisions on this thread; execution tickets for `App\Services\ProductReset\*` (4 services + trait + exception + migration + 2 CLI commands) can be sized.
- Browser / Dusk test scope — **resolved by #17**: out of scope Stage 1, re-evaluate when Stage 5 Federated Search UX lands.
- **CONTEXT.md revision**: ~15 SQLite-specific terms retire (Extension Connection Gate, Native Extension Fault, SQLite Extension Manifest, Extension Cache, Offline Extension Diagnostics, Extension Health Report, Extension Sync Command, Extension Fault Response, Diagnostic Correlation, SQLite Extension Verification Matrix, Native Extension Verification Matrix, Vector Capability Probe, Extension Support Matrix, Extension Diagnostics Command). Graduates as #40, #41, #42 resolve. Execution task tracked in bd. **After #40 + #41 + #42 (Postgres-pivot trio closed)**: ALL SQLite-specific terminology is now specifiable for removal — stack terminology (`sqlite-vec` → `pgvector`, `vec0 virtual table` → `HNSW index on vector(1536)`, `FTS5` → `tsvector + GIN with en_unaccent config`), schema organisation (`product-prefixed tables` → `product schemas with unqualified table names`, `chinook_artists` → `chinook.artists`), and the 14-term #12 framework (all dissolve, none transform). Retirement is now an execution-time cleanup task tracked in bd, no longer wayfinder-blocking.
- Acceptance Stage 2 ("Native SQLite extension capability on Herd and CI") in #11 transforms under Postgres into: `CREATE EXTENSION vector` (extversion ≥ 0.8.0), `unaccent`, and `pg_trgm` all succeed AND `CREATE SCHEMA chinook/northwind/sakila` succeeds on the Herd-managed Postgres :5437 service and on CI's `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` service; `en_unaccent` text search config present. Pest test `test_postgres_extensions_are_installed` gates the merge. The stage itself stays; gate content is now **fully specified** after #40 + #41 + #42.
- **Acceptance Stage 5 (Hybrid Search)** in #11 is now **fully specified** at the schema level after #32: each `*.search_projections` table exists with the pinned shape; `GENERATED ALWAYS AS … STORED` populates `document_tsv` correctly on source-row writes; HNSW + GIN indexes build; trigger maintains the projection on source CRUD; observer queues the embedding job on tier-1 writes; Baseline Invariant query (`embedding_state NOT IN ('complete','lexical_only')` count = 0) gates the end of Product Import / Reset. Detailed test shapes owned by #17 (test pyramid) + execution tickets. **After #28**: the observer-queue timing is refined — initial bulk-load staging suppresses the observer's queue path (trigger still writes the projection); rebuild phase post-publish queues + drains embeddings. Runtime CRUD post-go-live uses observer unchanged.
- **CONTEXT.md *Search Projection* term** now specifiable for revision after #32: current definition ("lexical representation is transactionally current; vector representation is derived after commit and independently verified") updates to reflect (a) lexical side is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS … STORED` (transactionally current by construction, no after-commit derivation), (b) vector side is async-tracked via `embedding_state` lifecycle (not "independently verified" — that defensive step is dropped, ACID covers it), (c) UUIDv7 Domain Identity is the projection PK directly (integer `search_id` bridge from #8 retires). Plus the 14 SQLite-specific terms from #12 already specifiable for removal after #40/#41/#42. All CONTEXT.md cleanup is now an execution-time task tracked in bd.

## Out of scope

- Re-opening any decision resolved in map #1 (#2–#13) without a recorded material reason (new upstream version, incompatibility discovered, etc.).
- Production hosting topology beyond the Herd macOS arm64 + Linux x86_64 CI targets named in the Two-Environment Operational Gate.
- Customer-facing music commerce, or merging the three sample domains into one shared business domain (carried over from map #1).
- The deferred product-facing Team Artefact experience with human-readable URLs and a slug policy (carried over from map #1).
- Separate physical database files or per-team clones of the sample datasets (carried over from map #1).
- A separate data warehousing/OLAP enhancement (carried over from map #1).
- **The SQLite Extension Connection Gate, Vector Capability Probe, Native Extension Fault, SQLite Extension Manifest, SQLite Extension Cache, Offline Extension Diagnostics, Extension Health Report, Extension Sync Command, Extension Fault Response, Diagnostic Correlation, Native Extension Verification Matrix, Extension Support Matrix, and Extension Diagnostics Command** concepts from decision #12 — all dissolved by the PostgreSQL pivot. `CONTEXT.md` retains the terms pending revision (graduates as #40, #41, #42 resolve).
- **The sqlite-vec v0.1.9 asset/digest verification and the Herd SQLite extension load-mechanism verification** — both dissolved by the PostgreSQL pivot. The #21 investigation established the finding #23 was sent to verify (Herd's stock PHP PDO cannot load sqlite-vec), which is what triggered the pivot to PostgreSQL + pgvector (#40); the sqlite-vec assets (#20) are no longer on the route. Closed: [#20](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/20), [#21](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21), [#22](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22), [#23](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/23).

items.title: Evaluate warehouse-as-config pattern from platform repo for inclusion
items.body:
## Context
The airflow-data-platform repository is being refactored to focus on core platform infrastructure that enhances Astronomer. During this refactor, we identified the `layer3-warehouses/` component that implements a valuable "warehouse as config" pattern.

## Component to Evaluate
**Source**: `airflow-data-platform/layer3-warehouses/`

## What This Pattern Provides
- **"Warehouse as Config"**: Define warehouse structure once, deploy to multiple environments
- **Environment abstraction**: Same warehouse definition works across dev/qa/prod
- **Connection management**: Integrates with Airflow/Astronomer connections
- **Multi-tenant support**: Different schemas/databases per environment

## Why This is Valuable
This pattern solves real enterprise problems:
1. Eliminates copy-paste errors between environments
2. Enables GitOps for warehouse definitions
3. Provides versioned warehouse schemas
4. Supports progressive deployment (dev → qa → prod)

## Evaluation Criteria
1. Is this pattern general enough for broad use?
2. How does it integrate with Astronomer's connection templates?
3. Should it be packaged as a plugin or library?
4. What examples would best demonstrate the pattern?

## Proposed Structure if Accepted
```
airflow-data-platform-examples/
└── warehouse-patterns/
    ├── README.md
    ├── warehouse-as-config/
    │   ├── config/
    │   │   ├── warehouse-dev.yaml
    │   │   ├── warehouse-qa.yaml
    │   │   └── warehouse-prod.yaml
    │   ├── dags/
    │   │   └── warehouse_sync_dag.py
    │   └── lib/
    │       └── warehouse_manager.py
    ├── multi-tenant-warehouses/
    └── cross-region-warehouses/
```

## Example Use Case
```yaml
# warehouse-config.yaml
warehouses:
  sales_dwh:
    type: snowflake
    database_pattern: "SALES_{ENV}"
    schemas:
      - bronze
      - silver 
      - gold
    environments:
      dev:
        account: dev-account.snowflake
        warehouse: XSMALL
      prod:
        account: prod-account.snowflake
        warehouse: LARGE
```

## Migration Tasks if Accepted
- [ ] Copy layer3-warehouses from platform repo
- [ ] Create clear examples with multiple warehouse types
- [ ] Document integration with Astronomer connections
- [ ] Show environment promotion workflow
- [ ] Add configuration validation
- [ ] Create migration guide from hardcoded to config-driven

## Decision Needed
This pattern adds significant value for enterprise deployments. Should it be included in examples, or does it deserve to be a standalone Astronomer provider plugin?

# Phase26 — Support Hub & Conversation Management

**Implementation-ready specification. All D1–D40 decisions and amendments are ratified; the founder confirmed the testing approach.**

Support Hub is one cohesive Asym surface with shared native CRM context and correctly authorized owner actions. This specification preserves the complete email/intake/work lifecycle, private collaboration, drafts and reading preferences, contextual guidance, safe file reading and recoverable Unwanted/future-mail holding journeys.

**Start with the user-story book**, then follow its stable US26/REQ26/AC26 identifiers into the detailed requirement volumes. The glossary fixes domain language; OpenSpec carries observable behavior, design and the unchecked implementation/qualification checklist. The source trace records every captured section's authority and disposition.

The full package contains **217 independently verifiable user stories, 2,210 detailed requirement definitions, 717 main OpenSpec scenarios, and all additional exact proof/operating-control suites**. It covers **all 40 ratified decisions**, including D27-C, D29-X01 and every accepted correction. Numerical limits, state/audience/source rules, failure recovery and release gates remain binding.

**Email Studio/P17** owns governed reusable content, canonical authoring and whole-message preparation. **P6** owns actual communication, provider evidence and recovery. **Support** owns human work, source-specific intent and private drafting; canonical intake owns receiving and held-mail decisions. CRM and giving/care domains retain their own truth, permissions and mutations. These seams are specified throughout the requirements, not left as integration assumptions.

**Confirmed proof approach:** real authenticated Support/API and canonical intake/job boundaries on disposable local Supabase; focused actual database permission/concurrency/migration proof; and full Playwright journeys on that same backend. Existing frameworks are reused and real-provider qualification stays separate.

No feature implementation or implementation-ticket graph is included. Specification/documentary validation has passed; product runtime, provider, accessibility, intended-user and release evidence remains required before activation. Local formal/OpenSpec mirrors are validated; this publication is the complete issue-tracker specification and does not claim a source PR.


**Complete version:** `phase26-ratified-spec-2026-09-15-v1` · manifest `9503ff46b1f85604d845c62a0045031cd1b43acb0e4b704c38a72ff6bfd205b8`.

The linked volumes below contain the complete specification and its declared traceability/evidence companions. Only volumes labelled normative define product requirements. They are not implementation tickets. All listed parts belong to this version.

items.title: sql: per-user/role/database resource limits (cpu,memory,concurrent queries)

labels.name: C-enhancement
labels.description: Solution expected to add code/behavior + preserve backward-compat (pg compat issues are exception)

items.body:
1.  FEATURE REQUEST

Feature: Allow user/role/database-based resource limits on CPU/memory usage, or limit the number of concurrent queries per user/role/database.

2.  Use case: In a multi-tenant application, there are often hundreds to thousands of users/applications being supported.  If the users have raw SQL access to the database, it is necessary to limit each one's resources to avoid performance issues.

This type of feature is quite common in the case of data warehouses, such as Teradata and Vertica which have to support thousands of users, but can't allow any particular user to hog all the resources due to a badly-written query.

3.  Nice to have.

Jira issue: CRDB-5735
